body:
The testing stack is ready.

It's composed of:
- karma
- mocha
- expect (assertions)

Changes in npm scripts:
- `test` now runs the tests in phantomjs and then lint
- `test:watch` will open a real chrome canary, output results in terminal console and auto reload tests

It's basically the stack from https://github.com/rackt/react-router/ with some modifications.

I wrote the `Hits` and `Template` tests, they may not be exhaustive but that's a start. Once we get this merged I will create the relevant issues so that anyone can help in writing tests.

We need to strengthen this library because untested code will and must #fail.

comments.body: Currently rewriting the previous tests to follow the same pattern

> Why did you choose components/**tests**/mycomponent.js over test/components/mycomponent.js?

So this is something I borrowed from the various famous react projects I looked at before doing our tests. Like react itself (https://github.com/facebook/react/tree/master/src/renderers/dom), react-router (https://github.com/rackt/react-router/tree/master/modules) and most rackt organization projects (https://github.com/rackt).

I found it handy and good because:
- tests are close to the implementation, in term of file organization
- you can cleary see if they are missing tests because if there's one missing test file then it's easier because there's less hierarchy to dig into
- we follow a convention that seems to get some traction in most react or not react based projects

It also look like what golang community is doing (file.go, file_test.go). Maybe we could directly take this road which is even better IMHO.

Good for you?

> It also look like what golang community is doing (file.go, file_test.go). Maybe we could directly take this road which is even better IMHO.

I generally don't put them too close because otherwise it's not clear where to put fixture/resource files that are used by tests (you clearly don't want to add them next to sources). Having the `__tests__` directory is OK if that's the "default/common" convention for React, the naming is just super weird -> it really looks like something auto-generated or that you shouldn't modify :/

> Having the **tests** directory is OK if that's the "default/common" convention for React, the naming is just super weird -> it really looks like something auto-generated or that you shouldn't modify :/

Yes at first look it seems weird I agree.

> I generally don't put them too close because otherwise it's not clear where to put fixture/resource files that are used by tests (you clearly don't want to add them next to sources).

I guess the golang community is no big fan of heavy fixtures or just put them inside the test file. If you know how to collapse code blocks with keyboard thats ok :D (ctrl+k[+0/1/2] in st)
